gbm_population_evidence.quote: WHO Grade 2-4 infiltrating glioma by histologic confirmation

candidate_evidence.quote: Solriamfetol is a wakefulness-promoting drug. Giving solriamfetol may improve sleep, memory, fatigue, mood, or quality of life in patients with brain tumors (gliomas).
Proportion With Grade 3 or Higher Adverse Events

treatment_setting_evidence.quote: Patients who are anticipated to undergo adjuvant chemotherapy are eligible as long as there is no evidence of tumor progression

Patients who are currently undergoing chemotherapy, targeted therapy, immunotherapy, or salvage treatment and have stable disease by imaging are eligible and can continue the current anti-cancer therapy.

role_evidence.quote: Solriamfetol in Improving Sleep in Patients With Grade II-IV Glioma

source_quote.quote: Where appropriate results from clinically available testing of isocitrate dehydrogenase (IDH) gene mutation status (for all gliomas)
MGMT gene promoter methylation status (for malignant gliomas) must be available in the patient's chart
chromosome 1p and 19q deletion status (for suspected oligodendrogliomas)

coder_notes: Solriamfetol is given for sleepiness/cognition/QoL; no antitumour hypothesis or outcome, so supportive and trial fails S6. Registered intervention name is misspelled 'Soliramfetol'. IDH, MGMT and 1p/19q results must be available in the chart but no particular status is required, so they are recorded as exploratory_correlative rather than eligibility biomarkers (no role fits exactly). Treatment setting coded both: patients after chemoradiation (adjuvant) and on salvage therapy are eligible.
